concepts.one_liner: Offline, printable reference tables mapping green coffee weight to expected roasted output by bean density and roast level, eliminating mental math during production reconciliation.
concepts.data_source_hint: Deterministic arithmetic on standard roast loss curves + World Coffee Research variety density data
concepts.source_pain: Cannot reconcile lot separation with café production stock
concepts.why_non_obvious: Pain served: Cannot reconcile lot separation with café production stock. Insight 2: Visual stock checks fail because roasters lack instant mental conversion between green input and roasted output. Evidence: User quote 'you roast say 10lb of Guatemala Coban and the inventory app updates taking into account... weight loss' shows the specific need is real-time conversion, not complex tracking. Wedge: Pure-computation product requiring zero external data or user accounts; unlike SaaS competitors (Cropster/RoasterTools) that require login/setup, this delivers immediate value via static indexable pages that rank for high-intent calculation queries while solving the reconciliation gap through education rather than software.
concepts.data_acquisition_notes: No external data required; arithmetic and user-configured/reference assumptions are local.

concepts.one_liner: Comparative substitution engine that ingests ICO price data, USDA production forecasts, and UN Comtrade trade flows to recommend functionally equivalent green-coffee substitutes when a roaster's spot coffee lot disappears or spikes in price, generating '[origin] coffee substitute' and 'blend gap filler' pages.
concepts.data_source_hint: ICO composite prices, USDA PSD production/stock forecasts, UN Comtrade bilateral trade flows — all official, bulk-downloadable datasets
concepts.data_route: ICO monthly price data (CSV download), USDA PSD (bulk CSV per commodity), UN Comtrade API (bulk extraction by HS code 0901)
concepts.source_pain: Cannot maintain café and subscription supply when spot coffee disappears
concepts.why_non_obvious: Pain served: Cannot maintain café and subscription supply when spot coffee disappears. Insight 3 — Green Coffee Supply Continuity and Lot Substitution: roasters already manually scramble through importer catalogs when a lot vanishes; no tool automates the substitution logic using trade-flow data that reveals what origins with similar cup profiles are actually flowing into their region right now. Evidence: 'But because of the poor state of the spot market it's a bad time to try to find a coffee for the gap' — this is a roaster actively searching for a substitute lot and failing. Wedge: The ICO+USDA+Comtrade data triad is public and bulk-obtainable but no coffee software ingests it for substitution logic; combining trade-flow velocity with origin/flavor-profile adjacency creates a recommendation engine that importer catalogs alone cannot replicate because importers only show their own inventory, not the full market picture.
concepts.data_acquisition_notes: ICO/USDA public downloads; Comtrade API/bulk files, with attribution and rate-limit constraints.

concepts.one_liner: A comparison tool that maps out-of-stock spot coffees to genetically and agronomically similar available beans using the WCR Varieties Catalog.
concepts.data_source_hint: World Coffee Research Coffee Varieties Catalog
concepts.data_route: World Coffee Research Coffee Varieties Catalog
concepts.why_non_obvious: Pain served: Spot coffee disappears. Insight 1: Co-op roasters chase 100-point scores but functionally need agronomic/genetic matches when a stable blend component runs out unexpectedly. Evidence: Buyers complain about the 'poor state of the spot market' making it a 'bad time to try to find a coffee for the gap.' Wedge: Inverting the public World Coffee Research Varieties Catalog to build a functional substitution matrix (matching genetic lineage and bean characteristics) provides a defensible data wedge that inventory tools like Cropster completely ignore.
concepts.data_acquisition_notes: WCR catalog is public but agronomic similarity is incomplete; availability requires first-party user input.

concepts.one_liner: Aggregates FDA import refusals for green coffee to provide an early-warning signal of spot market shortages before importers update their availability lists.
concepts.data_source_hint: FDA Import Refusal Reports (filtered for coffee HS codes)
concepts.why_non_obvious: Pain served: Spot coffee disappears. Insight 3: Spot coffee often disappears suddenly because a container is rejected at port for safety/defect reasons, leaving downstream buyers scrambling blindly. Evidence: Roasters specifically cite 'bad beans' (moldy, sour, insect) and 'debacles' with green coffee suppliers losing stock. Wedge: Aggregating FDA Import Refusal Reports for coffee provides a 1-to-2 week early-warning signal that an importer's lot failed customs, giving the user an actionable head start to buy alternative spot lots before the broader market realizes the container didn't land.
concepts.data_acquisition_notes: FDA refusal data is publicly downloadable/searchable; coffee HS filtering and shortage inference are noisy.

concepts.one_liner: A marketplace connecting micro-roasters struggling with small-batch margins to wholesale facilities offering idle production capacity for contract toll roasting.
concepts.data_source_hint: Self-reported idle capacity from commercial roasteries
concepts.source_pain: Cannot determine whether roasted coffee remains profitable after roast loss
concepts.source_segment: Wholesale Roasters Supplying Specialty Cafés and Restaurants
concepts.why_non_obvious: Pain served: Cannot determine whether roasted coffee remains profitable after roast loss. Insight 4: The stranded capacity marketplace gap. Evidence: 'Either you're inefficient with production or (more likely) you're not doing enough volume to get past your fixed costs.' Wedge: A two-sided marketplace bootstrapping supply by reaching out to commercial roasteries with large (15kg+) machines who want to monetize downtime, creating a structural advantage over software that just tells the micro-roaster they are losing money.
concepts.data_acquisition_notes: User-submitted capacity data; no public inventory index; marketplace cold-start and freshness risk.

concepts.one_liner: Lightweight Shopify app that auto-deducts green inventory based on roasted SKU sales using configurable yield ratios, bridging the gap between e-commerce orders and physical stock without full ERP.
concepts.data_source_hint: Shopify Orders API + Products API + Merchant-configured yield ratios
concepts.data_route: Shopify Partner API (official, documented, free for app developers)
concepts.source_pain: Cannot reconcile lot separation with café production stock
concepts.why_non_obvious: Pain served: Cannot connect roast logs to green inventory and customer orders. Insight 3: Disconnected systems force manual re-entry because roasters sell on Shopify but track production elsewhere. Evidence: Competitor gap analysis shows 'Disconnected Roast, Inventory, and Order Systems' as top frustration with 10 mentions; users explicitly name 'Google sheets, not connected' as pain point. Wedge: Platform API exclusivity — only Shopify-approved apps can access order/product webhooks in real-time; this creates a distribution advantage via App Store search plus solves the integration gap that standalone tools (Artisan/Cropster) cannot address without custom middleware, targeting the exact DTC micro-roaster segment already on Shopify.
concepts.data_acquisition_notes: Official authorized Shopify APIs/webhooks; merchant approval and app review/rate limits apply.

concepts.one_liner: Encodes the ISO 4072 green-coffee sampling protocol into a simple checklist that shared-space roasters can follow on receiving day, exporting a pass/fail PDF they can attach to every lot purchase order.
concepts.data_source_hint: Licensed ISO 4072 text plus simple arithmetic on user-entered defect counts
concepts.source_pain: Cannot reject defective green coffee reliably before committing to a lot
concepts.why_non_obvious: Pain served: Cannot reject defective green coffee reliably before committing to a lot. Insight 6: even operators who own ISO 4072 PDFs still copy the rules into spreadsheets each time a new crop arrives. Evidence: "temperature matters, how they’re stored matters, what happened before they arrived matters" (r/roasting). Wedge: the ISO text is licensed but static; wrapping it into a one-click checklist with auto-calculated defect thresholds is a 2-week solo build that none of the existing roast-log tools expose as a standalone module.
concepts.data_acquisition_notes: Uses user-entered counts and licensed protocol text; no external bulk data required.

concepts.one_liner: SaaS that imports weekly café POS or wholesale order CSVs, then back-calculates the exact green-coffee pounds and roast schedule needed to avoid stock-outs or over-roasting given typical loss rates.
concepts.source_pain: Cannot meet café volume without excessive roasting time
concepts.why_non_obvious: Pain served: Cannot meet café volume without excessive roasting time. Insight 5: Disconnected order data is the hidden bottleneck. Evidence: "Cannot connect roast logs to green inventory and customer orders". Wedge: Ingesting the exact CSV an operator already exports from their POS (or Shopify) removes any cold-start data problem and undercuts Cropster’s over-built forecasting module.
concepts.data_acquisition_notes: Users upload their own POS/order CSVs; no external bulk source or third-party access is required.

concepts.one_liner: Aggregates public FDA refusal codes and lot-level origin data into a shared-space roastery wiki so co-op members can log and query which importers repeatedly ship suspect green lots.
concepts.data_source_hint: FDA Import Refusal Reports + member-submitted lot annotations
concepts.data_route: FDA refusal CSV (public, downloadable); first-party user submissions
concepts.source_pain: Cannot reject defective green coffee reliably before committing to a lot
concepts.why_non_obvious: Pain served: Cannot reject defective green coffee reliably before committing to a lot. Insight 2: shared-space users already exchange defect stories verbally in Slack channels but never capture them for the next buyer. Evidence: "In specialty we often have lot separation for different farms, processes or even pick dates" (r/roasting). Wedge: first-party lot annotations from verified co-op members creates a self-reinforcing dataset that cannot be replicated by Cropster because its users work in isolation.
concepts.data_acquisition_notes: FDA refusal data is publicly downloadable; annotations require first-party submissions and moderation.
